finding: On any finite benchmark, every deterministic feature or relation computed from observed raw utterances can be encoded by a finite auxiliary variable U=index(L) or by its finite relation-signature class. Therefore the C010 requirement that raw-language structure survive every finite auxiliary-index representation is impossible to establish and cannot define language-specific identifiability.

counterexample.setup: Two latent causal models are equivalent on complete non-language trajectories and the finite benchmark utterance support; a proposed raw-string relation R is claimed to distinguish their latent partitions.
counterexample.collapse: Define U=(L,R(L)). Since the observed support is finite, U is finite, and any estimator using X,L,R can be rewritten using X,U with identical predictions and distribution on that support.
counterexample.consequence: Finite benchmark success cannot separate raw-language structure from unrestricted auxiliary indexing. Novelty requires restrictions on the auxiliary family and population-level out-of-support structure.

rejected_claim: Observable raw utterance relations eliminate a causal symmetry surviving complete trajectories and every finite auxiliary-index representation.
only_allowed_reformulation: Under a formal population grammar and a restricted auxiliary class that cannot copy utterance identity, test whether compositional relations among unseen utterance forms refine a known intervention-induced causal abstraction beyond complete non-language trajectories.
adoption_blockers: no benchmark split preventing utterance-identity lookup
